subject: ChartFlow — long-context eval plan & compliance items
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ChartFlow — long-context eval plan & model recommendations

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs
- Production use case: multi-visit clinical note consolidation + query summarization across patient histories (visit notes, attachments, audio transcripts).
- Target fidelity: preserve key events, medication changes, and problem-list items; high recall for allergies/meds.
- Typical document sizes: 50–400 pages (roughly 20k–250k tokens); many records are multi-file bundles (notes + pdfs).
- Compliance: ChartFlow requires HIPAA controls, data retention policy, and audit logs.

Proposed short-term evaluation (PoC)
1) Model shortlist to run quickly on Redwood hosted capacity:
   - Redwood-Instruct-34B-q4 (fast, quantized) — baseline for cost/latency
   - Llama2-70B-8k (higher-quality on instruction) — see tradeoffs below
   - LongForm-65B-64k (context-oriented variant) — for fidelity on >64k contexts
2) Evaluation axis: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity (ROUGE/QuestEval + human spot checks), hallucination rate on medication entities, latency and token cost.
3) Prompt sets: I attached the PoC data CSV (chartflow_poc_inputs.csv) — please add a small representative sample (2–3 patient bundles) if you want us to run an early run.
4) Timeline: initial automated runs within 5 business days after sample receipt; human review + summary within 2 weeks.

Known risks & mitigations
- Truncation: many models will drop oldest context when token window exceeded. Mitigation: run sliding-window summaries + prefix KV-cache approach; see Rishi’s notes (he’s cc’d).
- Summarization fidelity: for very long docs, we recommend chunked summarization with extraction of structured fields (meds/allergies) before free-text summarization.

Next steps (action items)
- ChartFlow: share 2 de-identified patient bundles (CSV + one PDF bundle) — Alex to confirm timeline.
- Redwood: provision a sandbox eval project, run three model variants, share benchmark links and a short readout.
- Schedule: technical deep-dive with engineering + procurement to discuss HIPAA/retention (suggest Wed Jun 2 or Thu Jun 3).

Attachments: chartflow_poc_inputs.csv (csv)
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cChartFlowEval

Thanks — Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChartFlow — long-context eval plan & model recommendations

Adding a few technical guardrails and an internal checklist. I ran quick spot tests last quarter on similar bundles; notes below are abbreviated.

Key observations from prior runs
- Models with fixed 8k windows (even 32k when emulated) start dropping earliest visits once context > window; this shows up as missing medication-start events in summaries ~15–25% of the time on clinical transcripts >50k tokens.
- 64k-capable models improve fidelity but still show compression artifacts when prompts include many repeated boilerplate sections (e.g., templated HPI).

Recommendations for PoC design
1) Input pipeline: canonicalize attachments into text, dedupe boilerplate sections, and tag structured entities (meds/allergies) before summarization.
2) Baseline prompts: create a two-stage flow — structured-field extractor (JSON output for meds/allergies/problem-list) followed by a contextual summary that references extracted fields. Prompt set A (attached to this email) covers both stages.
3) Truncation checks: run synthetic longer-than-production tests to trigger eviction behavior and capture token eviction logs. We should collect KV-cache traces to see what gets evicted.
4) Metrics: ROUGE-L, entity recall (manual), regression on safety classifier scores. Include a human-in-loop sample of 50 notes for qualitative checks.

Operational notes
- Cost estimate: rough hosted-run cost for 100 runs across 3 models ~ $7k–$12k depending on chunking/overlap. I’ll produce a tighter estimate after we know average token counts for the sample bundles.
- Compliance: for HIPAA PoC we should provision a dedicated sandbox instance in us-east-1 with customer-controlled key (bring-your-own-key) and retention TTL = 30 days by default. Procurement will want this spelled out in the SOW.

Attaching: long_context_eval_checklist.md (technical checklist & prompt templates)

Quotes from Neha’s message below for context:
> Production use case: multi-visit clinical note consolidation + query summarization across patient histories (visit notes, attachments, audio transcripts).

— Rishi
